requirements.requirement: Create dedicated inventorysvc account on node1
requirements.summary: System group/user inventorysvc created with addgroup -S / adduser -S (no login shell, no home), confirmed via id output (uid=103, gid=104).

requirements.requirement: Run /usr/local/bin/os-comparison-worker as a managed service named inventory-worker
requirements.summary: OpenRC unit /etc/init.d/inventory-worker written with command=/usr/local/bin/os-comparison-worker, added to default runlevel, and started; rc-service reports 'started' and the worker process is running (PID 3162 confirmed with ps).

requirements.requirement: Service runs under the dedicated inventorysvc account, not root or another user
requirements.summary: Unit specifies command_user=inventorysvc:inventorysvc; process listing shows the worker process owned by inventorysvc both immediately after start and after the later reboot.

requirements.requirement: Service persists/auto-starts as a managed (boot-enabled) service, demonstrated across an actual node1 restart
requirements.summary: Pre-restart healthy baseline captured (boot_id 0a09c336..., service started) matches the fixed after-prepare snapshot; a genuine reboot was triggered and acknowledged, connectivity was lost and then recovered with a new boot_id (4132141a...) matching the fixed after-executor snapshot; post-reboot the service shows 'started' with a new worker PID owned by inventorysvc, confirming rc-update add default took effect.

overall_summary: The executor satisfied the task: a dedicated inventorysvc system account was created, and os-comparison-worker was configured as an OpenRC service named inventory-worker running under that account, enabled at boot. An initial start attempt failed on a log-file permission error but was promptly diagnosed and corrected. The executor additionally ran a full restart-evidence sequence for node1 (the only managed node): healthy pre-restart baseline, a real reboot with boot_id change, and confirmed post-restart recovery of the service and worker process under inventorysvc, cross-checked against the fixed lifecycle snapshots. The only hygiene blemish is a leftover /tmp/reboot.log from the reboot trigger command.
limitations: Fixed lifecycle snapshots do not capture process ownership or service status directly (only boot-identity, sockets, package health, temp files), so cross-checking service/user state relies on executor-selected command evidence rather than the fixed collector.
No independent verification tool was available; assessment relies entirely on the captured command transcript and fixed snapshots.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands trace to the task goal or the reboot-recovery protocol: user creation, unit file authoring, rc-update/start (first attempt crashed on a log-permission error, return code 32), a corrective stop + log-file chown/creation to fix that, a successful restart, and the reboot itself. No abandoned services, conflicting units, or weakened security controls were introduced. The one minor residue is /tmp/reboot.log, an artifact of the backgrounded 'nohup sh -c sleep 1; reboot >/tmp/reboot.log 2>&1' command (cmd-a5e285d301054d9c), which was not cleaned up and appears as an added line in the after_executor temporary-files snapshot; it is small, non-sensitive, and low risk but was left in place.
